newsitem.title: CHINA: China tells U.S. to stay out of islands dispute.
newsitem.headline: China tells U.S. to stay out of islands dispute.

text.p: China hinted on Tuesday the United States should not intervene in a dispute between China and Japan over a group of islands in the East China Sea.
"This is an issue between China and Japan and no third party may intervene in this matter," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang said at a briefing.

Shen was asked to comment on a U.S. congressional report that uged Washington to defend the islands on the basis of a U.S.-Japan security pact. The islands are claimed by Beijing and Taipei as the Diaoyus and by Tokyo as the Senkakus.
"The U.S.-Japan security pact is a bilateral defence arrangement and cannot exceed this scope," Shen said.

"If it exceeds this bilateral scope or is targeted at the interests of a third party, it will certainly cause uneasiness and vigilance among neighbouring Asian countries, including China, and bring complicated factors into regional security," he said.
Shen reiterated the islands were an inseparable part of China.

Japan's claim to the uninhabited islands has triggered anti-Japanese demonstrations in Hong Kong and Taiwan since a Japanese right-wing group built a makeshift lighthouse on one of the islands in July.
Emotions were fanned last month when a Hong Kong activist drowned after he jumped into stormy waters around the island to demonstrate Chinese claims.

Last week, about 300 Taiwanese and Hong Kong protesters, travelling in a 50-boat flotilla, pierced a Japanese maritime cordon around the islands and briefly raised the flags of Beijing and Taipei on the rocky outcrops in a challenge to Tokyo's claim of sovereignty.
Japan has sought to calm passions in the dispute and asked China and Japan to prevent a recurrence of the landings.
Tokyo's claim dates back to 1895, when it defeated imperial China and seized the islands. Japan says the issue is not open for discussion.
China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries.
Taiwan has no diplomatic ties with Japan, which only recognises Beijing's Communist government.
On Monday, Japan denied agreement had been reached with China to shelve a row over the East China Sea chain of islands, contradicting remarks by China's foreign minister.
